title: He went for a TV and came home with a dog
author: Storytime
hook: My husband got up at four in the morning to buy a TV on Black Friday. He came home with a dog instead.
story: My husband Tom has been obsessed with one TV deal for a month. Sixty-five inches. Half price. Doors open at five. He set three alarms. At four this morning, he kissed my forehead and left. At nine, he texted me, don't be mad. At ten, the front door opened. No TV. Instead, a very old, very grey dog walked in, wagging his whole body. Tom said, there was a shelter adoption event in the parking lot. He's been there for three hundred and twelve days. Nobody wanted him because he's eleven. Then Tom got quiet. He said, he looks just like Buster. Buster was our dog. He died in March. Tom never cried about it. Not once. But he was crying in our hallway now. He said, I stood in line for the TV for two hours. Then I looked over and he was just sitting there, looking at me. The TV sold out anyway. The shelter told Tom the dog's name is Pickles. He wants to keep the name. I'm not sure about Pickles. Help us. What should we name him?
caption: the best Black Friday deal was free 🐶 #storytime
sound: a soft, heartwarming acoustic guitar at very low volume
why: Posted on Black Friday, the TV versus dog swap is instantly shareable, the late dog Buster adds emotion, and asking viewers to name him pulls tons of comments.

title: Grandma took my uncle's bet
author: Storytime
hook: At Thanksgiving yesterday, my uncle bet a hundred pounds he's never been wrong in his life. My grandma took the bet. And won.
story: Every family has one. Ours is my uncle Clive. He corrects everyone. Your recipe is wrong. Your car is wrong. Your career is wrong. Yesterday, at Thanksgiving dinner, after correcting my cousin about how to carve a turkey, he said, I'll bet a hundred pounds to anyone at this table. I have never been wrong. Not once in my life. Everyone groaned. And then my grandma, who's eighty-seven, put down her fork and said, I'll take that bet. She went to her bedroom and came back with an old envelope. Yellow. Stamped nineteen eighty-six. She handed it to Clive. It was a letter, in his own handwriting, written when he was nineteen. To his mum. It said, I'm never getting married. Marriage is a trap. I'll never have kids. And I'll never, ever move back to this town. Clive has been married for thirty years. He has four kids. He lives two streets from Grandma. The whole table exploded. Clive just stared at the letter. Then he quietly handed Grandma a hundred pound note. And for the rest of the night, he didn't correct anyone. Should we frame the letter?
caption: grandma kept the receipts since 1986 ✉️ #storytime
sound: a cheeky, triumphant orchestral sting at very low volume
why: Thanksgiving dinner aftermath stories peak today, every family has a know-it-all, the 1986 letter is a hilarious receipt, and the frame it question invites funny comments.

title: My manager raised prices before Black Friday
author: Storytime
hook: On Monday, my manager told me to raise prices on half the store. Today, Black Friday, those items are fifty percent off.
story: I work at a home goods store. Last Monday, my manager, Doug, handed me a list. Two hundred items. He said, go raise these prices. Some by forty percent, some by double. I asked why. He said, so the Black Friday discounts look better. Don't overthink it. I did it. But I took a photo of every single price tag before I changed it. Old price, new price, date. All of them. This morning, the doors opened at six. Huge signs. Fifty percent off. People were thrilled. A woman at my register was buying a blender. Fifty percent off. She asked me, is this really a deal? I hesitated. Then I showed her the photo on my phone. Same blender, last Sunday. Nineteen dollars cheaper than her deal price. She didn't get angry. She just smiled, took out a business card, and said, thank you. I'm the regional director. I've been visiting stores undercover all week. Doug was standing right behind me. I could hear him breathing. She asked me to email her every photo. I have three hundred and forty. Should I send them?
caption: the fake sale had receipts 🏷️ #storytime
sound: a tense retail beat with a satisfying reveal sting at very low volume
why: Fake Black Friday discounts are trending today, the photo log is the planted detail, the undercover regional director twist is satisfying karma, and should I send them drives comments.
